mail.subject: Good luck with the new venture!
mail.body:
Hello love,

Your uncle says you can have the garage as long as you need it — just keep the bike out of the rain and don't touch his paint tins.

I've told everyone at the WI you fix computers now. Mrs Okafor's grandson needs a laptop for college, so make sure you sell him a good one.

Kettle's in the corner. Proud of you.

Pat x

mail.subject: How this works — read me first
mail.body:
1. PURCHASING: buy a lot of ex-corporate laptops. Cheap lots are cheap for a reason (more faults, more wear). The lorry brings it next morning.

2. HAUL: carry laptops in from the pallet on the drive (up to 3 at once). Hover over a unit to see its cosmetic condition.

3. TEST: put a unit on the test bench and plug in the DiagnostiKit USB. It runs by itself — go and do something else. Testing is always accurate.

4. REPAIR: faulty units go to the repair bench. Hold E to fix. You need the right part in the parts bins (order in the Shop — it comes with the courier).

5. IMAGE: swap the bench USB for the PaneOS USB to wipe and install a fresh OS.

6. GRADE: hold E at the grading desk. A/B/C/D depends on wear and battery health.

7. SELL: shelve it, list it on Flogit. Price below guide = sells faster.

8. SHIP: when it sells, pack it at the packing table and put the box on the OUTGOING shelf before the courier comes (12:00 and 16:30).

Rent is due every Friday. Don't let the cash run dry.

mail.subject: Tips for new sellers
mail.body:
Welcome to Flogit!

• Buyers love fair prices. Listings at or below the guide price sell much faster.
• Grade honestly. Accurate grades build your seller rating.
• Dispatch on time — late parcels cost you rating, and a buyer who waits too long will cancel.
• Spares/Repairs listings sell quickly to tinkerers, but for much less.

Happy selling!
The Flogit Team

mail.subject: Refresh season
mail.body:
Alright,

Heard you've gone into refurb. Tip: big organisations swap kit on a schedule — banks every 3 years, schools every 2, that logistics lot every year. Check the refresh calendar in your purchasing app and keep cash back for the big lots.

Also: never trust 'sold as seen'. Half of those have had the drives pulled.

G
